subject: Follow-up: tenancy segmentation proposal, procurement gates, and SLA asks
messages:
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@medgrid.ai>, Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@medgrid.ai>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: tenancy segmentation proposal, procurement gates, and SLA asks

Hi Samira / Tom — thanks again for the productive call today. Quick recap and the immediate asks so we keep momentum: 

Summary of pain & goals
- Pain: inconsistent inference latency at scale for multi-tenant inference (peaks during batch uploads), tight data isolation needs for PHI workloads, and unpredictable token costs when models spike.
- Goals: a predictable committed capacity path (reserved pool), strict tenant isolation for PHI workloads (VPC + encrypted KV cache), and an SLA envelope that lets you certify platform performance for clinical pipelines.

Redwood proposal (high level)
- Reserved baseline: 60 A100-equivalent GPU baseline (dedicated pool) sized for steady-state throughput.
- Burst: shared burst capacity up to +40% for short-term peaks (governed by burst credits and pre-warm policies).
- Isolation options we discussed: (A) fully isolated pool (dedicated nodes, SAN/VPC peering), (B) tenant-slicing with hardware-backed isolation (vGPU + network ACLs), (C) hybrid where PHI jobs go to isolated pool and non-PHI use a lower-cost shared variant.
- SLA targets we've tentatively set: P50 token latency < 50ms, P95 < 120ms (for generation with typical 512-token contexts) and a 99.9% uptime objective for the dedicated pool. We will bake in graceful fallback to a compatible model variant if a node becomes unavailable.

Operational notes & recommendations
- KV cache pre-warm + prefix caching for your hot prompt surface will reduce steady costs by ~15-25% (we'll share a profile-based suggestion).
- Quantization: for retrieval-heavy pipelines we recommend int8 variants for burst capacity to reduce cost; we can validate on a short workload sample.

Immediate asks from MedGrid
1) Procurement contact and PO cadence (who will manage PO / billing)?
2) Security gate: confirm whether your security team needs SOC2 artifacts and whether a Network Diagram + IAM controls are sufficient for initial review.
3) Workload sample: a 48h sample (token/sec and request distribution) so our sizing spreadsheet can finalize GPU-equivalents.

Next steps (proposed timeline)
- Today: I’ll send the segmentation options PDF and a sizing worksheet (attached).
- By Tue (2027-04-13): MedGrid provides a sample workload and procurement contact.
- Week of 4/19: technical deep-dive (SRE + your infra) to finalize isolation topology and finalize SLA wording for PO.

Attachments: tenancy-segmentation-options.pdf, redwood-sla-draft-v2.docx, sizing-estimate-MG-2394.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll be standing by to schedule the technical follow-up once you have the workload sample.

— Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0137

Date: 2027-04-12T09:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: tenancy segmentation proposal, procurement gates, and SLA asks

Lauren / Samira — quick technical notes from my side after reviewing the recording: 

1) Workload sizing: if MedGrid can provide a 48h trace we’ll run a small simulation to validate the baseline GPUs vs burst sizing. The attached sizing spreadsheet has fields for 99th request size, average token/sec, and spike cadence.

2) Isolation details: for PHI we recommend the fully isolated pool (option A) with customer VPC peering + CMK-managed encryption for KV cache. We’ll also include a runbook for failover to a non-PHI-compatible fallback to preserve availability during maintenance windows.

3) Kernel/quantization note: If the model is a decoder-only LLM with long-context (>= 2k) we will surface different kernel selection and the expected latency curve — please mark that in the workload sample.

4) Ops SLA asks: we can commit to the 99.9% uptime on the dedicated pool with scheduled maintenance windows and a 30-minute escalation response for Sev1 incidents. Final SLA wording is attached (redwood-sla-draft-v2.docx).

I’ll take point on the sizing run if MedGrid sends the trace — happy to run it in our sandbox and share a TLDR.

— Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com

Attachments: sizing-estimate-MG-2394.xlsx
From: Samira Khan <samira@medgrid.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@medgrid.ai>, Kelly Monroe <kelly.proc@medgrid.ai>
Date: 2027-04-12T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: tenancy segmentation proposal, procurement gates, and SLA asks

Thanks Lauren and Priyom — solid summary. A few items from our side: 

- Procurement: looping in Kelly (cc’d) — she’ll own the PO timeline and contract review. Our procurement window is end of May; we’re hoping to align commercial terms by then.
- Security: our InfoSec team will want SOC2 Type II evidence and a network diagram. I’ll get back with an exact list but expect a 5-business-day review once we share the initial artifacts.
- Workload sample: we can export a 48h trace but will need a short anonymization pass. Kelly, can procurement share the contact who manages data exports?

As for the technical choices, we’re leaning to hybrid: isolated pool for PHI inference and tenant-slicing for analytics/telemetry jobs. That said, we need a final cost estimate comparing hybrid vs fully isolated. Can Redwood produce a delta per month for the two modes?

Also curious on billing granularity — do you invoice monthly for reserved capacity and separately meter burst? That will affect our PO structure.

— Samira
CTO | MedGrid AI
samira@medgrid.ai
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@medgrid.ai>, Kelly Monroe <kelly.proc@medgrid.ai>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: tenancy segmentation proposal, procurement gates, and SLA asks

Thanks — Kelly, great to meet you. Quick answers: 

- Billing cadence: reserved capacity is invoiced monthly on committed spend; burst usage is metered and billed as an overage line item (itemized per-day). We can produce a sample invoice format for PO review.
- Cost delta: we’ll prepare a three-row comparison (fully isolated, hybrid, tenant-slicing) with committed baseline and expected burst overage ranges. Priyom will run the delta once we have the 48h token trace.
- Docs & security: attaching the SOC2 summary link and the network diagram draft; Samira, please confirm if that is sufficient for your InfoSec triage — we can augment with the audit log retention policy if needed.

Next call: I’m proposing a 30–45 minute technical alignment on Thu 2027-04-15 at 10:00 PT (SRE + MedGrid infra + Priyom). If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and a short agenda.

Action items
- MedGrid: share workload trace (QA/anonymized) and procurement contact (Kelly) — target 4/13.
- Redwood: cost-delta doc + sample invoice format + final SLA wording for legal — target 4/15.

If those timelines look good I’ll send the invite now.

Best — Lauren
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
